title: Linen handling, bed preparation and guest amenities
audience: Short-stay turnover cleaners handling linen, preparing beds and replenishing amenities.
learningOutcomes: Separate used and clean linen, and inspect used linen for sharps and contamination before handling.
Sort and launder linen by the care labels and the property policy.
Replenish amenities from the approved inventory, and report shortages and defects.

instruction.heading: Used linen: containment before handling
instruction.body: Used linen is handled as a containment task first and a laundry task second. Before you touch it, put on the gloves the task requires, and any other PPE the business procedure sets. Stand the bag open next to the bed, not on a clean surface. Inspect the linen before you lift it: look for sharps such as needles or broken glass, and for visible contamination. Do not reach blindly into pockets or folds. If you find a sharp, stop, do not remove it by hand, and tell the coordinator so that the item can be dealt with by the approved route. Gather the linen from the outside inwards, and do not shake it, because shaking spreads particles and any contamination into the air and onto clean surfaces. Place it in a designated bag and close the bag. Heavy contamination, such as bodily fluid in quantity, and any suspected infectious material are not routine linen. Escalate them to the coordinator and follow the business procedure rather than handling them yourself. Wash your hands after the task, and after you remove the gloves.

instruction.heading: Sorting, care labels and laundering
instruction.body: Sort the linen by the approved fabric and colour groups, and read the care label on each item before you load it. Use the temperature, the cycle and the drying setting the label and the property policy allow. Use only the detergent or product that the approved procedure names, and never improvise an additive such as a bleach or a fabric treatment. Keep chemicals apart, because mixing two products can create a hazard, and follow the label and the SDS for each one. Do not overload the machine beyond its rated load, and report any machine fault, leak, unusual noise or smell to the coordinator instead of working around it. If you cannot read a label, do not guess; set the item aside and ask the coordinator. Record any item that has been damaged or stained during laundering.

instruction.heading: Making up beds
instruction.body: Clean your hands before you handle fresh linen. Check each mattress and pillow protector for tears, stains and fit, and use the correct size for the bed. Fit the protector flat and smooth, then the sheets, pillowcases and cover in the order the property standard sets. Avoid dragging clean linen across the floor, and keep it off surfaces you have not cleaned. Check the bed from the guest's point of view: the corners are square, the surface is clean, there are no hairs or marks, and the linen is free of creases the standard does not allow. Count the linen for the room against the inventory, and record any shortfall.

instruction.heading: Amenities from the approved inventory
instruction.body: Replenish towels, toiletries, toilet paper, kitchen consumables and welcome items only from the approved inventory sheet, and use the products and containers the sheet names. Check each item for a sealed pack, an intact label, a readable expiry date where one applies, and cleanliness. Place items as the presentation standard shows. Never refill an unlabelled or unapproved container, and never use personal products from home. Where an item is near its expiry, or its seal is broken, remove it and report it. Count the consumables against the sheet, and report any shortage, damage or missing stock separately from the linen count.

instruction.heading: The handover check and reporting
instruction.body: Finish with a handover check that covers the beds, the linen count, the amenities and any stain or damage. A stain on a mattress protector or a missing item is not solved by covering it. Isolate the item, mark it so that it cannot be used, and report it with its location, the time and a description. Record the defect and the shortage in the handover, even when the shortage has been made up from another room, so that the coordinator can see the true stock position.

procedure: Put on the PPE the task requires, and stand the bag open next to the bed before handling the linen.
Inspect used linen for sharps and visible contamination before you lift it, and do not reach blindly into folds.
Stop and escalate any sharp, heavy contamination or suspected infectious material, and follow the business procedure.
Gather the linen from the outside inwards, do not shake it, and bag it in the designated bag.
Sort and launder by care label and approved setting, using only the approved products, and report any machine fault.
Clean your hands, check the protectors, fit the clean linen correctly, and avoid dragging it across floors.
Replenish amenities from the approved inventory, and check seals, expiry dates and cleanliness.
Count linen and consumables, and report defects, stains, damage and missing stock without covering them.

workedExamples.situation: After making two beds, a cleaner finds a stained mattress protector and only one spare.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What do you do with the stained protector, and what do you record?
workedExamples.reasoning: Isolate the stained item and mark it so that it cannot be used. Do not cover it with clean sheets, and do not wash it in a sink outside the approved procedure. Tell the coordinator about the stain and the shortage, and ask for the spare to be replaced or the bed made up another way. Record the defect, the time, and the stock shortfall in the handover.

workedExamples.situation: While gathering used linen, a cleaner feels something sharp inside a pillowcase.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What do you do before you touch it again?
workedExamples.reasoning: Stop. Do not reach into the pillowcase to remove the object, and do not shake the linen. Keep the bag closed and leave it in place if it is safe to do so. Tell the coordinator, who will direct the approved route for the sharp. Record what was found and where, and wash your hands and any exposed skin once the task is paused, as the procedure directs.

workedExamples.situation: A cleaner has run out of the usual bottled shampoo and finds an unlabelled refill bottle in the cleaning cupboard.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What do you put in the guest bathroom, and what do you report?
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not use the unlabelled refill, and do not use a personal product from home. Use only the product the approved inventory names. If none is available, report the shortage, and record that the amenity was not replenished. Do not replace it with an unapproved product to make the room look complete.

equipmentAndPpe: Gloves and task-appropriate PPE, as set by the business procedure and the SDS of any product used.
Designated linen bags, closed and labelled for used linen.
Care label reference card and the approved laundry settings sheet.
Approved inventory sheet for amenities and consumables.
Approved products with their labels and SDS available. Containment, such as closed bags and sealed bins, comes before PPE in the control order.
Marker or tag for isolating a stained or damaged item.

commonErrors.prevention: Gather the linen from the outside inwards and bag it without shaking.

commonErrors.error: Reaching blindly into pockets or folds of used linen.
commonErrors.prevention: Inspect before lifting, and stop and escalate any sharp.

commonErrors.error: Covering a stain with clean linen.
commonErrors.prevention: Isolate the item, mark it, and report it.

commonErrors.error: Refilling an unapproved or unlabelled container.
commonErrors.prevention: Use only approved containers and products from the inventory sheet.

commonErrors.error: Overloading the machine or improvising a laundry additive.
commonErrors.prevention: Load within the rated load, use the approved product, and report any machine fault.

commonErrors.error: Dragging clean linen across the floor.
commonErrors.prevention: Carry clean linen clear of the floor and keep it off uncleaned surfaces.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Heavy or suspected infectious contamination is escalated and not handled as routine linen.

Chemicals. Products must be used under the label and the SDS. Safe Work Australia's guidance says the SDS must be easy for workers who use or handle the chemical to reach. A business that has hazardous chemicals at a workplace should keep a register listing each with its current SDS, kept where workers can reach it.

Control order. Safe Work Australia's risk-management code places containment and other controls above PPE, and describes PPE as a last resort or a back-up to higher controls (copy dated December 2011, section 4.1; a later edition was not read).
Laundry equipment. Machine loads, settings and fault handling follow the equipment's own instructions and the property policy.

qualityStandard: Used linen is bagged without shaking, and any sharp or heavy contamination is stopped and escalated in the simulation.
Beds are made up with clean hands and correctly fitted linen, and the linen is kept clear of the floor.
Amenities come only from the approved inventory, and each one is checked for seal, expiry and cleanliness.
Stains, damage and shortages are reported and isolated, and none is covered or concealed.
documentationEvidence: Linen and stock count record, with the shortfall marked.
Defect and shortage report with location, time and description.
Record of any sharp or heavy contamination found and escalated.
summary: Keep used and clean linen apart, inspect before you lift, and never shake used bedding.
Launder by the care label and the approved setting, and report any machine fault.
Use only approved amenities, and report stains and shortages without covering them.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why must used bedding not be shaken?
options: It is heavy to lift and awkward to carry in one go from the bed
It tears the fabric when it is pulled out of the bed frame
It can spread contamination into the air and onto clean surfaces

knowledgeChecks.question: A stained protector is found and there is no spare. What is correct?
options: Isolate the stained item and report it to the coordinator
Cover it with clean sheets for the next guest to use tonight
Wash it in the sink with the hand soap and rinse it

knowledgeChecks.question: Which products may be used for amenities?
options: Any products from home that the cleaner prefers
Only approved products from the inventory
Refills from unlabelled bottles in the van

knowledgeChecks.question: What must be read on each item of linen before it is loaded?
options: Nothing, the load is sorted by colour only
